text:
OF CHRIST, BOOK III.

But many are deaf to my voice, and stubborn. Most people listen to the world more willingly than to God: they follow the desires of their own flesh more easily than the good pleasure of God. The world promises temporal and small things, and is served with great greed: I promise the highest and eternal things, and the hearts of mortals grow sluggish. Who serves and obeys me with such care in all things as the world and its masters are served? <margin>Isaiah 23</margin> Blush, O Sidon, says the sea. And if you seek the reason, hear why. For a small stipend, a long journey is taken; for eternal life, many hardly lift a foot from the ground once. A cheap price is sought; sometimes people quarrel shamefully for a single coin; for a vain thing and a small promise, they do not fear to toil day and night.

4. But, oh the shame! For an unchangeable good, for an invaluable reward, for the highest honor and endless glory, one is lazy about toiling even a little. Blush then, you slothful and complaining servant, that those people are found more ready for destruction than you are for life. They rejoice more in vanity than you do in truth. Indeed, they are sometimes frustrated in their hope; but my promise deceives no one, nor does it send away empty those who trust in me. What I have promised, I will give; what I have said, I will fulfill, provided that one remains faithful in my love until the end. I am the rewarder of all good people, and a strong examiner of all who are devoted.

5. Write my words in your heart, and ponder them diligently; for they will be very necessary in the time of temptation. What you do not understand when you read, you will recognize on the day of visitation. I am accustomed to visit my chosen ones in two ways, namely, by temptation and by consolation. And I read two lessons to them daily: one, by rebuking their vices; the other, by exhorting them to the growth of virtues. He who has my words, and scorns them, has one who will judge him on the last day.

<summary>This passage contrasts the human tendency to prioritize fleeting worldly gains over divine promises, and explains that God uses both temptation and consolation to refine the faithful.</summary>
<keywords>divine service, temptation, consolation, eternal life, faithfulness, judgment</keywords>
